gates.description: Events must be named in past tense (OrderPlaced, not CreateOrder)
Event schema must include event_id, event_type, aggregate_id, timestamp
Events must include correlation_id and causation_id for tracing
Consumer idempotency strategy must be documented
Dead letter queue strategy must be defined for failed events

anti_patterns.description: Every small change emits an event — hundreds of event types, most consumed by nobody
Events that tell consumers what to do: SendEmailEvent, UpdateCacheEvent
Events with huge payloads containing every field from every system
Events with no way to trace them back to the original trigger
Events never deleted, storage grows forever, replay takes hours

escalation_triggers: Event ordering guarantees required across different aggregate types
Event replay needed but volume makes it impractical without infrastructure changes
A consumer consistently failing to process events and DLQ growing without resolution
Event schema change breaks backward compatibility and consumers cannot be updated simultaneously
Business requires exactly-once processing but infrastructure only guarantees at-least-once

output_certifications: Event schemas defined with required fields (event_id, event_type, aggregate_id, timestamp)
Events named in past tense using business language
Correlation and causation IDs included in schema
